title: Group Discussion
description: Win the GD round: stake a position, build on and challenge others, facilitate, and drive a group to consensus. B2 to C1.

nodes.title: Stake a Clear Position
nodes.skill: Open on a debate topic with an unambiguous stance in one or two sentences.
nodes.teach_focus: Commit to a side; avoid fence-sitting; state the position before the reasons.
nodes.success_criteria: A clear, committed position on the topic, stated up front without hedging.

bridge_exercises.sentence: On this topic, I ___ that remote work helps companies more than it hurts them.
bridge_exercises.hint: a verb that commits you to a side
bridge_exercises.context: Drills the opening verb that signals a committed stance rather than a hedge.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: believe

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which opening stakes the clearest position?
bridge_exercises.hint: pick the one that commits to a side with no hedging
bridge_exercises.context: Trains the learner to spot a committed stance versus fence-sitting.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: I'm firmly in favour of banning single-use plastics.
options: I'm firmly in favour of banning single-use plastics.
Well, it's hard to say, there are points on both sides.
Maybe plastics are an issue, I suppose, sort of.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Topic: 'Social media does more harm than good.' Open the discussion by stating your position in one sentence before any reasons.
bridge_exercises.hint: lead with your stance, not a question or a hedge
bridge_exercises.context: Free production of a committed, position-first opening under a live topic.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Expected elements: position-first opening, clear commitment to one side, and no hedging or question opener.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which opening commits to a side while leaving room for nuance?
bridge_exercises.hint: clear side first, qualification second
bridge_exercises.context: Helps the learner avoid fence-sitting while still sounding mature.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: I support making remote work the default, with planned in-person moments for trust and onboarding.
options: I support making remote work the default, with planned in-person moments for trust and onboarding.
Remote work has advantages and disadvantages, so it depends.
I am not sure because both sides have points.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Open a GD on a topic you care about. Commit to one side in one sentence, then add one guardrail or condition.
bridge_exercises.hint: position first, condition second
bridge_exercises.context: Pressure variant for a clear opening that is decisive without becoming simplistic.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Expected elements: clear position plus one guardrail or condition that makes the stance more mature without fence-sitting.

exemplars: On this topic, I believe a four-day work week would raise productivity, not lower it.
My position is clear: schools should teach financial literacy as a core subject.

nodes.title: Support With Evidence
nodes.skill: Back a position with a relevant fact, example, or analogy — not just assertion.
nodes.teach_focus: Position -> because -> concrete support; prefer specifics over generalities.
nodes.success_criteria: A stance followed by at least one relevant, concrete piece of support.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Cities should expand bike lanes. ___, Amsterdam cut car traffic sharply after doing exactly that.
bridge_exercises.hint: a two-word phrase that introduces a concrete example
bridge_exercises.context: Practises the signal phrase that turns a bare claim into supported reasoning.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: For instance

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which reply backs the stance with the most concrete support?
bridge_exercises.hint: look for a specific fact or example, not a repeated opinion
bridge_exercises.context: Teaches the learner to recognise concrete support over re-asserted opinion.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Online courses widen access — for instance, that free coding platform now reaches two million rural learners.
options: Online courses widen access — for instance, that free coding platform now reaches two million rural learners.
Online courses widen access because they are genuinely very good at widening access.
Online courses widen access, and I really do feel strongly about that.

bridge_exercises.sentence: State your position on 'Electric cars are better for the planet,' then support it with one concrete fact, example, or analogy.
bridge_exercises.hint: say your stance, then 'because' or 'for instance' and one specific detail
bridge_exercises.context: Free production of the position-then-concrete-support pattern.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Expected elements: stance followed by one concrete fact, example, or analogy; avoid repeating the opinion as evidence.

exemplars: Remote work boosts output — for instance, our team shipped 20% more after going hybrid.
I'd back stricter privacy laws; after the EU passed GDPR, companies finally started deleting data they didn't need.

nodes.title: Enter the Discussion
nodes.skill: Break into an ongoing discussion politely and claim speaking space.
nodes.teach_focus: Signal phrases to interject; assertive but not rude; link to what was just said.
nodes.success_criteria: A polite, well-timed entry that connects to the prior speaker and adds something new.
nodes.bridge_focus: Use one entry phrase: 'If I could add to that, ___.'

bridge_exercises.sentence: If I could ___ to that, I think the cost angle matters just as much as the time saved.
bridge_exercises.hint: a verb meaning to contribute something extra
bridge_exercises.context: Drills the polite entry stem used to claim the floor.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: add

bridge_exercises.sentence: The group is mid-flow. Which entry is polite, well-timed, and links to the last speaker?
bridge_exercises.hint: assertive but not rude, and it should connect to what was just said
bridge_exercises.context: Contrasts a graceful interjection with abrupt or self-centred ones.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Building on what Riya just said, could I add a quick point about cost?
options: Building on what Riya just said, could I add a quick point about cost?
Stop — let me talk now, I've been waiting.
Anyway, forget all that, here's a completely different topic.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Two people are debating whether exams should be scrapped. Interrupt politely, link to the last point, and add something new.
bridge_exercises.hint: use an entry phrase, acknowledge them, then add your point
bridge_exercises.context: Free production of a well-timed, linked entry into a live discussion.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Expected elements: polite entry phrase, link to the prior speaker's point, and one new relevant contribution.

exemplars: If I could add to that, the same logic applies to small businesses, not just large firms.
Just to jump in on Sam's point — there's a related risk we haven't mentioned yet.

nodes.title: Build on Another's Point
nodes.skill: Extend a point someone else made, crediting them and adding new value.
nodes.teach_focus: Acknowledge -> extend -> add; collaborative tone that raises group quality.
nodes.success_criteria: A contribution that credits the prior speaker and meaningfully extends their idea.
nodes.bridge_focus: Finish: 'Building on what ___ said, we could also ___.'

bridge_exercises.sentence: Building ___ what Maya said about cost, we could also factor in long-term maintenance.
bridge_exercises.hint: the preposition that goes after 'building'
bridge_exercises.context: Fixes the acknowledge-then-extend frame at the connector level.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: on

bridge_exercises.sentence: Someone said 'free transport would cut emissions.' Which reply credits them AND adds new value?
bridge_exercises.hint: it should name or echo their idea, then push it further
bridge_exercises.context: Distinguishes genuine building-on from mere agreement or hijacking.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: That's a strong point on emissions — and it would also help low-income commuters most.
options: That's a strong point on emissions — and it would also help low-income commuters most.
Yeah, I agree, totally agree, good point.
Forget emissions, my real concern is parking.

bridge_exercises.sentence: A peer just said 'remote work saves commute time.' Credit them, then extend the idea with something new.
bridge_exercises.hint: acknowledge, then add a fresh angle they didn't mention
bridge_exercises.context: Free production of the credit-then-extend collaborative move.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Expected elements: credit the prior speaker, extend their idea, and add new value rather than merely agreeing.

exemplars: Building on what Priya said, we could also extend that incentive to first-time renters, not just buyers.
That ties nicely into Dev's point — and it suggests the policy would pay for itself within a year.

nodes.title: Disagree Respectfully
nodes.skill: Challenge another participant's point without attacking the person.
nodes.teach_focus: Concede something valid -> state the counter -> keep it about ideas.
nodes.success_criteria: A disagreement that concedes a fair point, states a clear counter, and stays civil.
nodes.bridge_focus: Use: 'That's fair, but I'd push back because ___.'

bridge_exercises.sentence: That's a fair point, ___ I'd push back, because the cost falls hardest on small firms.
bridge_exercises.hint: a soft contrast connector
bridge_exercises.context: Gives a ready frame for conceding then disagreeing without attacking.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: but

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which reply disagrees most respectfully?
bridge_exercises.hint: concede something valid first, then keep it about the idea
bridge_exercises.context: Moves from a frame to choosing tone under realistic phrasing.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: You make a fair point on speed — though I'd argue the rushed rollout is exactly what caused the bugs.
options: You make a fair point on speed — though I'd argue the rushed rollout is exactly what caused the bugs.
That's just wrong and you clearly haven't thought it through.
No. That makes no sense at all.

bridge_exercises.sentence: A peer argues 'AI will replace most teachers within a decade.' Disagree respectfully: concede a fair point, then state your counter.
bridge_exercises.hint: validate something true, then push back on the idea, not the person
bridge_exercises.context: Free production of the concede-then-counter civil disagreement.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Expected elements: concede one fair point, counter the idea rather than the person, and keep a civil GD tone.

bridge_exercises.sentence: I agree with the concern about speed, ___ I think safeguards matter more here.
bridge_exercises.hint: soft contrast connector
bridge_exercises.context: Practises disagreeing through ideas instead of blunt rejection.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: but

bridge_exercises.sentence: A peer says, 'This policy is obviously the fastest option.' Disagree respectfully by conceding speed, then naming the safeguard risk.
bridge_exercises.hint: concede speed, then counter with risk
bridge_exercises.context: Pressure variant for challenging an overconfident participant without sounding hostile.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Expected elements: concede speed or another valid benefit, then name the safeguard risk as the counter-point.

exemplars: I hear you on cost, but if we delay we lose the whole quarter — so I'd still ship now.
That's a fair concern, though I'd argue the data points the other way on safety.

nodes.title: Present a Balanced View
nodes.skill: Weigh both sides of the topic, then land on a reasoned position.
nodes.teach_focus: Acknowledge the strongest opposing point honestly before concluding; show nuance.
nodes.success_criteria: A nuanced contribution that fairly states a counter-argument and still reaches a clear conclusion.
nodes.bridge_focus: Name one point for each side, then say which is stronger.

bridge_exercises.sentence: There are real costs to remote work, but ___ I think the flexibility outweighs them.
bridge_exercises.hint: a two-word phrase meaning 'considering everything'
bridge_exercises.context: Practises the connector that pivots from weighing sides to a verdict.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: on balance

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which contribution is genuinely balanced — fair to the other side yet still conclusive?
bridge_exercises.hint: it must honestly grant the opposing point, then still decide
bridge_exercises.context: Separates true nuance from one-sided takes and pure fence-sitting.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Stricter rules do slow innovation, I'll grant that — but on balance, the safety gains are worth the trade-off.
options: Stricter rules do slow innovation, I'll grant that — but on balance, the safety gains are worth the trade-off.
Stricter rules are simply good and there's no real argument against them.
Honestly both sides are equally right, so I can't really choose.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Topic: 'Should homework be abolished?' Name one fair point for each side, then say which is stronger and why.
bridge_exercises.hint: grant the opposing side honestly before you land your conclusion
bridge_exercises.context: Free production of weigh-both-sides-then-conclude reasoning.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Expected elements: one fair point for each side, a clear final verdict, and the reason that side is stronger.

exemplars: Critics are right that the policy is costly; still, weighing both sides, the long-term savings make it worth it.
There's a real case for speed, but on balance I think doing it carefully matters more here.

nodes.title: Steer a Derailed Discussion
nodes.skill: Redirect a discussion that has drifted off-topic back to the core question.
nodes.teach_focus: Name the drift neutrally; restate the actual question; offer a refocusing point.
nodes.success_criteria: A move that gently flags the drift and pulls the group back to the original topic.
nodes.bridge_focus: Use: 'We've drifted a bit — the real question is ___.'

bridge_exercises.sentence: I think we've ___ a bit — the real question is whether the budget should grow at all.
bridge_exercises.hint: a verb meaning to wander off the topic
bridge_exercises.context: Drills the neutral phrase that names the drift before refocusing.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: drifted

bridge_exercises.sentence: The group has wandered onto office snacks instead of the hiring policy. Which move steers back best?
bridge_exercises.hint: flag the drift neutrally, then restate the actual question
bridge_exercises.context: Contrasts a graceful redirect with blame or simply ignoring the drift.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: These tangents are fun, but let's loop back — the question on the table is how we should change hiring.
options: These tangents are fun, but let's loop back — the question on the table is how we should change hiring.
Why does everyone keep going off-topic? Focus, people.
Sure, let's keep talking about snacks, that's fine.

bridge_exercises.sentence: The topic is 'Should city centres ban cars?' but the group is now arguing about football. Steer them back without blaming anyone.
bridge_exercises.hint: name the drift gently, restate the real question, offer a refocusing point
bridge_exercises.context: Free production of a neutral, well-judged redirect.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Expected elements: neutral drift marker, restatement of the real topic, and one concrete refocusing point.

exemplars: We've drifted a bit — the real question is whether the policy actually reduces emissions.
Good tangent, but let's refocus: are we for or against the proposal on the table?

nodes.title: Bring In Quieter Voices
nodes.skill: Invite a silent participant into the discussion to show facilitation skill.
nodes.teach_focus: Notice who hasn't spoken; invite without pressure; reference the topic for them.
nodes.success_criteria: A natural, specific invitation that opens space for a quieter participant.
nodes.bridge_focus: Use: 'I'd like to hear ___'s take on this.'

bridge_exercises.sentence: I'd like to ___ Neha's take on this — she's been quiet but I'm sure she has a view.
bridge_exercises.hint: a verb meaning to listen to someone's opinion
bridge_exercises.context: Practises the warm invitation stem for drawing in a quiet member.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: hear

bridge_exercises.sentence: Sara hasn't spoken yet. Which invitation is natural, specific, and pressure-free?
bridge_exercises.hint: warm and specific to the topic, not a demand or a spotlight grab
bridge_exercises.context: Separates a gracious invitation from pressure or a generic prompt.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Sara, you've worked in retail — I'd love your take on how this affects shop staff.
options: Sara, you've worked in retail — I'd love your take on how this affects shop staff.
Sara, you haven't said anything, so go ahead, say something now.
Does anyone else want to talk, anyone at all?

bridge_exercises.sentence: In a discussion on minimum wage, one person hasn't spoken at all. Invite them in naturally, referencing the topic for them.
bridge_exercises.hint: name them, tie it to the topic, leave room to decline
bridge_exercises.context: Free production of a specific, low-pressure invitation.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Expected elements: name the quiet participant, connect the invitation to the topic or their experience, and leave room to decline.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Neha, you've been quiet on the customer-impact side; I'd like to ___ your view if you want to add.
bridge_exercises.hint: invite without pressure
bridge_exercises.context: Practises a specific invitation that leaves room to decline.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: hear

bridge_exercises.sentence: A quiet participant has relevant experience but has not spoken. Invite them in naturally, connect to the topic, and avoid putting them on the spot.
bridge_exercises.hint: name them, connect to their angle, leave space
bridge_exercises.context: Pressure variant for facilitation without spotlight pressure.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Expected elements: low-pressure invitation that connects the quiet participant's angle to the active discussion.

exemplars: I'd like to hear Aman's take on this — he mentioned earlier he'd seen it firsthand.
Leena, you've stayed quiet on the cost side — what's your read on that?

nodes.title: Manage a Dominant Speaker
nodes.skill: Tactfully reclaim the floor from someone monopolizing the discussion.
nodes.teach_focus: Validate briefly -> interrupt cleanly -> hand off; assertive without hostility.
nodes.success_criteria: A polite but firm move that pauses the dominant speaker and redistributes the floor.
nodes.bridge_focus: Use: 'That's a strong point — let's also hear other views.'

bridge_exercises.sentence: That's a strong point, Karan — let's also ___ what others think before we move on.
bridge_exercises.hint: a verb meaning to listen to / find out
bridge_exercises.context: Drills the validate-then-redistribute phrase for pausing a dominator.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: hear

bridge_exercises.sentence: One person has talked for three minutes straight. Which move reclaims the floor firmly but without hostility?
bridge_exercises.hint: validate briefly, interrupt cleanly, then hand off to the group
bridge_exercises.context: Contrasts a tactful reclaim with rude cut-offs and passive silence.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Those are great points, Vik — let me pause you there so we can bring others in.
options: Those are great points, Vik — let me pause you there so we can bring others in.
Vik, you talk way too much, give it a rest.
(say nothing and let him keep going)

bridge_exercises.sentence: A participant keeps cutting others off and dominating the GD on climate policy. Reclaim the floor and hand it to the group.
bridge_exercises.hint: acknowledge their point, interrupt cleanly, then pass it on
bridge_exercises.context: Free production of an assertive, non-hostile floor-reclaiming move.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Expected elements: brief validation, clean pause or interruption, and redistribution of the floor without hostility.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Those are useful points, Vik; let me ___ you there so we can bring in another view.
bridge_exercises.hint: a polite interrupt verb
bridge_exercises.context: Practises pausing a dominant speaker without attacking them.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: pause

bridge_exercises.sentence: A participant keeps interrupting others. Validate their point, pause them, and hand the floor to someone else in one or two sentences.
bridge_exercises.hint: validate -> pause -> redistribute
bridge_exercises.context: Pressure variant for assertive facilitation under a tense GD moment.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Expected elements: validate the dominant speaker's point, pause them firmly, and hand the floor to another voice or the group.

exemplars: That's a strong point — let me pause you there so we can also hear from the others.
I appreciate the detail, Sid; in the interest of time, let's open it up to the rest of the group.

nodes.title: Summarize and Drive Consensus
nodes.skill: Synthesize the group's points into a summary that moves toward a shared conclusion.
nodes.teach_focus: Capture the main threads fairly; name common ground; propose a conclusion.
nodes.success_criteria: A concise synthesis of the discussion's key points plus a proposed consensus the group can rally around.
nodes.bridge_focus: Name the two main points raised, then propose where the group agrees.

bridge_exercises.sentence: So to ___: most of us agree on the goal, and we mainly differ on the timing.
bridge_exercises.hint: a two-word verb meaning to give a brief summary
bridge_exercises.context: Practises the closing stem that signals a synthesis is coming.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: sum up

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which closing best synthesizes the discussion and proposes a consensus the group can rally around?
bridge_exercises.hint: capture the main threads fairly, then name the common ground
bridge_exercises.context: Distinguishes a true synthesis from a one-sided or vague ending.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: We've heard strong cases for both speed and safety — and we all seem to agree on a phased rollout, so let's propose that.
options: We've heard strong cases for both speed and safety — and we all seem to agree on a phased rollout, so let's propose that.
Anyway, I was right all along, so let's just go with my idea.
We talked about a lot of stuff, so let's stop here.

bridge_exercises.sentence: The GD on 'four-day work week' is ending. Summarize the two main points raised and propose where the group can agree.
bridge_exercises.hint: fairly capture both threads, name common ground, propose a conclusion
bridge_exercises.context: Free production of a fair synthesis that drives toward consensus.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Expected elements: fair summary of two main threads, named common ground, and a proposed consensus the group can accept.

exemplars: So to sum up: we agree the goal is worth it, and the main open question is timing — let's propose a phased start.
We've heard two big threads — cost and fairness — and the common ground seems to be a pilot first, then a full rollout.
